title: Multi-Model Route Split Billing and Ephemeral Cache Credit Job
creator: Jana Patel
description:
Problem: Our current billing pipeline attributes cost at the per-request model level, which misses two important cases: 1) multi-model routing where a single user request fans out to multiple model variants (e.g., reranking => small model + large model) and 2) ephemeral KV / prefix cache credits consumed during short-circuit responses. This ticket implements a batch job (transform + enrichment + attribution) to normalize multi-model route splits and emit per-tenant, per-route, and per-model attribution rows that include cache_credit consumption and fallback tagging.

Goals:
- Unify cost attribution for requests that touched multiple models into a single atomic attribution row with split percentages and an audit trail.
- Account for ephemeral cache credits (prefix/KV cache reads) separately so cached tokens are not double-billed to model inference.
- Produce output compatible with downstream billing-rollup worker (release: billing-2026.02) and analytics dashboards.
- Fail-safe: when metadata is missing, fall back to route-level attribution and emit an explanatory tag for downstream reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Nightly run produces normalized attribution table with columns: tenant_id, request_id, route_id, model_variants:[model,split_pct,cost_estimate], cache_credits, total_tokens, timestamp, source_tags. 2) Sample of 10k requests reconciles to existing raw ledger within +/-0.5% after mapping rules. 3) Downstream billing-rollup accepts the new schema without errors in staging. 4) There is a clear audit trail linking original model calls (model_call_id) to the attributed row.
implementation_notes:
Architecture:
- Input: streaming token ledger (kafka topic: token-ledger-v2) + model-call metadata (call metadata topic) + KV cache telemetry (cache-reads topic).
- Staging layer: de-dup + windowed-join by request_id using Flink job with 30s event-time window.
- Enrichment: apply routing rules from route-config store (redis / config service) to decide priority splits for heuristics where explicit split percentages are missing.
- Attribution logic: compute token-weighted cost per model variant, subtract cache_credit token counts from charged tokens, emit normalized row to BigQuery table billing_attribution.normalized_routes.
- Observability: emit per-run metrics (processed_requests, failures, emited_rows, percent_fallback).

Performance constraints:
- Job must process ~4M requests/day in staging; target latency for a single request attribution: < 2 minutes for nearline flows.

Notes:
- Use existing token-cost map maintained by ENG-19845 for per-model unit price.
- Persist a compact audit blob (gzipped JSON) for first 90 days for forensic queries.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for split math and cache subtraction logic with edge cases (zero tokens, 100% cache hit, missing model metadata).
- Integration tests in staging by replaying a 48h window of kafka topics and validating reconciliation metrics vs historical ledger.
- Canary run against 1% of tenant traffic with shadow writes to new table; compare with baseline attribution for divergence alerts.
- Load test to validate Flink parallelism knobs (target 50k events/s).
- QA checklist: schema migration backward compatibility, idempotency for replays, handling late-arriving events.
rollback_plan:
- If we detect >1% divergence in sample checks or errors >0.5% during canary, pause new job and switch downstream consumers to legacy attribution table.
- Job runs are idempotent by request_id; reprocess after fix by replaying Kafka topic from checkpointed offset.
- Communicate to billing ops and customer success with timeframe and affected tenants list (generated from job logs).
